title: A finitely generated idempotent ideal is generated by an idempotent
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. (1) If $I\subseteq R$ is a finitely generated ideal with $I^2=I$, there is an idempotent $e\in R$ ($e^2=e$) with $I=eR$. (2) If $e\in R$ is idempotent and $\psi:R\to T$ is a surjective ring homomorphism with $\ker\psi=(1-e)R$, then $\psi(e)=1$, and the ring map $R_e=R[1/e]\to T$ induced by $\psi$ is an isomorphism; that is, $T$ (via $\psi$) is a localization of $R$ at $e$. In particular $R/(1-e)R\cong R_e$.
